$comment: Human-curated corrections to OSM station naming. Every entry records WHY it exists,
because a future maintainer must be able to tell a real correction from a guess.

nodeNames.$comment: OSM nodes that carry no `name` tag at all. Without these the station silently vanishes from the graph — a whole missing station, not a cosmetic defect.

631525335.name: Matunga Road
631525335.reason: Node has name:hi (माटुंगा रोड) and ref=MRU but no `name` tag. It is a real Western Line station between Dadar and Mahim Junction, and its absence would break Western Line adjacency.
631525335.evidence: OSM node 631525335, tags IR:zone=WR:CCG, ref=MRU, railway=stop; position 19.02816,72.84673 falls between Dadar and Mahim on the Churchgate–Virar sequence.

$comment: Parenthetical and trailing qualifiers that exist only to disambiguate OSM nodes and
must not reach the user. Applied to build the DISPLAY name.
Order matters: these are applied as written.
stripSuffixes.$bracketedNote: OSM disambiguates shared-name metro platforms with square brackets, e.g. 'Dahisar (East) [Line 2]' / '[Line 7]' / '[Line 9]' — three nodes for ONE interchange. Only brackets whose contents match these patterns are stripped. NOTE: the parenthetical '(East)' is deliberately KEPT — 'Dahisar East' (Metro) and 'Dahisar' (Western Line) are different stations and must not collapse.

displayNames.$comment: Full replacements where stripping is not enough, or where the local common name differs from OSM's.

Mumbai CSMT (Suburban).name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus
Mumbai CSMT (Suburban).reason: OSM's parenthetical is an internal qualifier. The full official name is used for display, with CSMT as the short form and both searchable.

Mumbai Central (local).name: Mumbai Central
Mumbai Central (local).reason: '(local)' distinguishes the suburban platforms from the long-distance terminus; not meaningful to a commuter planning a suburban trip.

Vadala Road.name: Wadala Road
Vadala Road.reason: OSM uses the 'Vadala' transliteration; 'Wadala' is the spelling used on station boards and by Indian Railways. Both are searchable via aliases.

$comment: Search-only synonyms. These make search forgiving without merging distinct stations.
Transliteration variance (v/w, single/double letters) is handled HERE by explicit alias
rather than by fuzzy folding in name_norm, because aggressive folding risks colliding

normStopWords.$comment: Words removed when building name_norm for MATCHING only. Never removed from display names. 'Junction' is dropped so 'Kalyan' matches 'Kalyan Junction'.

doNotMerge.$comment: Normalised names that must NEVER resolve to a single station. The clustering rule already requires proximity and a shared operator, so this is a belt-and-braces assertion: if upstream data ever drags these together, the build fails. A false merge silently corrupts every route and fare through the station. Checked by asserting no cluster with this norm exceeds maxClusterSpreadM.

names.reason: Western Line Naigaon (19.3521N) and Monorail Naigaon (19.0095N) are unrelated stations ~38 km apart sharing a name. Name-only matching would fuse the Western Line to the Monorail.
names.note: LIVE as of 2026-08-06: the Monorail is now curated in, so this guard is exercised — 'naigaon' correctly resolves to 2 separate stations (Western Line 19.3521N, Monorail 19.0095N).

names.reason: Matunga (Central Line) and Matunga Road (Western Line) are different stations 362 m apart. They already differ after normalisation, but if a name edit upstream collapsed them the fare for any route through them would be wrong.

forceMerge.$comment: Station complexes the automatic rule misses because their platforms are spread further apart than the 250 m merge radius. The radius stays tight on purpose — widening it globally is how you fuse unrelated stations — so these are explicit, reviewed exceptions. Same operator only. Verified 2026-08-06 against out/interchange-candidates.json.

groups.reason: Santacruz Western Line and Harbour Line platforms are one station complex, measured 255 m apart — 5 m outside the default radius.
Jogeshwari Western and Harbour corridor platforms are one station; OSM stop nodes sit 563 m apart along a long station footprint.
